title: Hard bound: source-resident plus batched/fused Q8_0 after combined correctness

interpretation.correctness_status: CPU-compatible Q8_0 arithmetic is proven token-stable for combined up/down on the fixed France verifier.
interpretation.per_call_status: The current per-call implementation is too slow and remains rejected as a performance path.
interpretation.top768_status: Top768 fits the previously measured roughly 3.2 GiB extra-pool shape, but its zero-overhead bound is only 6.48 tok/s. It can be considered only as an intermediate SOTA candidate, not a 10 tok/s design.
interpretation.top3072_status: Top3072 nearly reaches 10 tok/s with zero overhead, but needs 12.75 GiB payload and still has negative 73.955 ms slack before kernel/scatter/sync overhead.
interpretation.top4096_status: Top4096 is the first positive 10 tok/s zero-overhead bound, but requires 17.0 GiB payload before gate cache/workspace, so it does not fit the current VRAM allocation while preserving gate behavior.

decision.reason: The smallest near-10 payload is at least 12.75 GiB with no overhead slack, and the first positive 10 tok/s bound needs 17.0 GiB. Current extra usable VRAM with gate cache preserved is about 3.2 GiB.
do_not_do: Do not implement a large source-resident top768 path as a claimed 10 tok/s route.
Do not rerun the slow per-call Q8_0 strict cold benchmark.
Do not sacrifice gate cache for a topN pool unless a new bound includes the resulting gate miss penalty and still exceeds the acceptance gate.
allowed_next: A top768 resident batched path may be planned only as an intermediate SOTA candidate with a separate cost/TTFT bound.

For the 10 tok/s goal, the next candidate must reduce payload footprint, avoid needing resident raw source for thousands of experts, or remove CPU fallback time through a different exact batching/microkernel path.
